This is Palmo One. We are under siege. We're being slaughtered. The Imperial murder of Ghorman has begun. There are hundreds of bodies this moment. As I say these words, hundreds of murdered Ghormans lay dead in Palmo Plaza. Thousands more on the streets. More every minute. We're being destroyed! If you believe in truth, if you have any faith left in truth, please, please mark this message and pass it forward. This is murder! The Empire built this fire. They made this fire and led us to the slaughter. Now they expect us to die without knowing why. The conspiracy we've feared is real! It's here today!|[[Dreena]]|}} The '''Ghorman Massacre''', also known as the '''massacre on Ghorman''' or the '''Imperial murder of Ghorman''', was a pivotal moment in the [[Imperial Era]] that occurred in [[2 BBY]] when [[Imperial Army]] forces violently suppressed peaceful protests on the [[planet]] [[Ghorman]], opening fire on multitudes of peaceful civilians. The massacre, which [[Death|slaughtered]] hundreds if not thousands of protesters according to the [[Imperial Archives]], was part of the [[Galactic Empire]]'s escalating crackdown on [[Early rebellion against the Galactic Empire|insurgent activity]] within [[the galaxy]], and was also an inciting moment for the [[Galactic Civil War]]. In response to the massacre, [[Senator]] [[Mon Mothma]] of [[Chandrila]] made an address in the [[Imperial Senate]], which explicitly called out the incident as genocide against the Ghorman people and publicly laid blame on [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], branding him a "lying executioner." Declared a traitor as a result and hunted by the [[Imperial Security Bureau]], Mothma went into exile and delivered the [[Declaration of the Rebel Alliance]]. This unified the fragmented rebel cells and solidified the Rebel Alliance, with Mothma as its [[Chancellor (Rebel Alliance)|leader]], escalating the fight against the Empire. The massacre convinced many sympathetic to the rebels that peaceful opposition to the Empire was not tenable, which catalysed open civil war that ultimately led to the Empire's [[Battle of Jakku|demise]]. Such was the extent of the mobilization caused by the massacre, that the historian [[Beaumont Kin]] would later prescribe the event as "a serious miscalculation" on the part of Imperial officials within his the history book, ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''. The Memorial to the Missing of Ghorman was later established to honor the victims, many of whom would remain unknown to history given the sheer death toll brought about by the Empire's actions during the [[Imperial Era]]. ==Prelude== ===The Tarkin Massacre=== {{Main|Tarkin Massacre}} {{Quote|Sixteen years ago, Grand Moff Tarkin killed 500 peaceful, unarmed Ghormans in the middle of that plaza.|Carro Rylanz in 3 BBY, to Cassian Andor|}} In [[19 BBY]],{{Andor|Ever Been to Ghorman?}} shortly after the [[Proclamation of the New Order|proclamation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], protests emerged on the [[planet]] [[Ghorman]], in the capital city of [[Palmo]]. During the unrest, [[Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] attempted to land his [[cruiser]] on a landing pad, only to be met by protesters flooding the area in the hopes of preventing his arrival. Tarkin brought the ship directly down upon the protesters,{{Andor|I Have Friends Everywhere}} killing five-hundred of them in an event that became known as the [[Tarkin Massacre]]. A memorial, the [[Monument to the Fallen]], was built to commemorate the casualties of Tarkin's actions. ===Early Resistance=== {{Quote|There will be a fact-finding commission put in place this session. And it will prove that this is a boot to the throats of all Ghormans who've done nothing more than request their basic rights.|Senator Mon Mothma of Chandrila, speaking on behalf of the people of Ghorman|}} [[File:Imperial_Senator_Mothma-Andor.png|thumb|left|250px|Senator Mon Mothma of Chandrila, speaking before the Imperial Senate during the Ghorman Debates]] In the [[Standard year|years]] that followed, local militias and insurgencies—including the [[Ghorman Front]]{{Andor|Narkina 5 (episode)}}— cropped up to oppose the Empire's [[The galaxy|galactic]] rule.{{Rebels|Call to Action}} To counter the [[Early rebellion against the Galactic Empire|emerging rebellion]], the [[Imperial Security Bureau]] was tasked with hunting down and eliminating insurgent threats.{{Andor|Aldhani (episode)}} The [[Imperial Senate]], meanwhile, had become largely ineffective in curtailing Imperial overreach, although some [[senator]]s, such as [[Mon Mothma]] of [[Chandrila]],{{Andor|Announcement}} nonetheless tried to wield their influence to support those in need, including the [[Ghorman (people)|people]] of [[Ghorman]] who had requested that the Empire honor their basic rights{{Andor|The Eye}} during the Senate's [[Ghorman Debates]]. Senator Mothma worked in secret with other like-minded individuals, such as [[Luthen Rael]] and Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]] of [[Alderaan]],{{Databank|rebel-alliance|Rebel Alliance}} to [[Axis network|fund and organize]] a network of various rebel cells and insurgent movements in the hopes of growing their influence and effectiveness against the Empire. The Ghorman Front also became known to early rebels like Rael and [[Saw Gerrera]] of the [[Partisans]]. ===A Secret Meeting=== {{Main|Ghorman project|Maltheen Divide conference}} In [[4 BBY]], Director [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]] of the [[Imperial Military Department of Advanced Weapons Research]] held a [[Maltheen Divide conference|meeting]] with high ranking [[imperial officer]]s at the [[Maltheen Divide]]. During the meeting, Krennic outlined a [[Ghorman project|plan]] to [[Gouge mining|gouge mine]] [[Ghorman]] for the precious and rare mineral [[kalkite]], which was needed for the [[Darth Sidious|Galactic Emperor]]'s "[[Project Celestial Power|Energy Project]]".{{Andor|One Year Later}} During the meeting, Krennic questioned [[ISB Supervisor|ISB supervisor]] Dedra Meero about how she would approach the project, to which she suggested instigating an anti-Imperial insurgency on Ghorman, so that the Empire would gain a legitimate reason to suppress any resistance on the planet. Impressed by the suggestion, Krennic subsequently placed Meero in charge of the project. Despite being reluctant at first, Meero eventually agreed to run the project at the persuasion of [[major]] [[Lio Partagaz]]. ===The Ghorman program=== {{Main|Suppression of Ghorman}} Around [[3 BBY]] [[Syril Karn]], who was secretly partners with Dedra Meero, was reassigned from Coruscant to [[Ghorman]] to lead the local division of the [[Imperial Bureau of Standards]]. In fact, he became by that moment an undercover ISB operative with a task to make contact with Ghorman Front. He helped them — with ISB approval — to procure weapons and proofs of hostile Imperial activity on the planet. However, Karn wasn't aware of the real aim of the Ghorman operation as he had thought that he was to catch the outside agitators. ==The Ghorman Massacre== ===Bad luck Ghorman=== {{Quote|There is, apparently, no suitable replacement or synthetic alternative for the Ghorman substrate material.''"
"''I see.''"
"''It's not for lack of effort. Krennic's had the lab in Eadu working overtime all year. I don't know the science, but… it's bad luck Ghorman. We need what's in the ground, and when we're done, there won't be much left to call 'home.'|Lio Partagaz and Dedra Meero|audio=Partagaz-Meero-BadLuckGhorman-OneYearLater.flac|{{Andor|Messenger (episode)}}}} By [[2 BBY]], during the early days of the [[Galactic Civil War]],The {{Databank|url=mustafar-history-gallery|text=Mustafar History Gallery}} states that the [[action at Mustafar]], which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates to [[4 BBY]], was one of the earliest rebel victories in the [[Galactic Civil War]]. Therefore, the Galactic Civil War must have begun by 4 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]. {{EncyclopediaCite|The Birth of the Rebellion}} states that the Galactic Civil War, which ended in [[5 ABY]] according to ''Star Wars: Galactic Atlas'', lasted nine [[Standard year|years]], meaning that it must have begun in 4 BBY. This places it ahead of the Ghorman Massacre, which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[2 BBY]]. the fledgling rebel network had drawn the attention of the Imperial Security Bureau with operations on worlds such as [[Aldhani]], [[Ferrix]],{{Andor|Rix Road (episode)}} and [[Lothal]].{{Rebels|Fire Across the Galaxy}} That year, peaceful protests on Ghorman would quickly escalate into large crowds of Ghormans facing off with Imperial forces.{{ProductionBrief/Andor2}} More pressingly, the Ghorman Front had procured a large number of Imperial weapons. Secretly however, the ISB had manipulated the front's actions to radicalize the Ghorman people to justify imperial presence, which could eventually lead to the silencing of the planet and allow [[mining]] of the planet. [[File:Noalternative.png||thumb|right|250px|Major Partagaz informed Meero that mining on Ghorman was to proceed]] On the day after an alleged [[Firebombing at the Imperial Naval Terminal|firebombing]] of the [[Imperial Naval Terminal]] in [[Palmo]], ISB [[major]] [[Lio Partagaz]] informed the now-Ghorman Project head [[Dedra Meero]] that the "energy project"'s [[Eadu Energy Conversion Laboratory|lab]] on [[Eadu]] had failed to find alternatives to [[Kalkite]] for the project, so Ghorman mining was to proceed. To assure that the situation was properly dealt with to facilitate Imperial mining of the planet, Dedra was given permission to [[Declaration of Martial Domain|declare martial law]] and stroke a conflict on Ghorman; while the operation was identified as a resettlement plan,{{InsiderCite|233|Andor Season 2 Companion|''Andor'' Season 2 Companion}} the Imperial efforts were designed to bring forth civilian causalities in an act that would later be described as genocide. To assist in these efforts, army captain [[Kaido]], a crisis specialist, was sent to Ghorman assume tactical command of Imperial forces located there. ===''Gambol dum Ghor''=== {{Quote|We are the Ghor! The galaxy is watching!|Ghorman protest chant|audio=WeAreGhor.mp3|}} Following Kaido's arrival, a fleet including mining ships arrived in the [[Ghorman system]] to begin [[gouge mining]] Ghorman. The Empire began landing [[mining rig]]s and [[Mining droid|droids]] at Ghorman locations such as [[Leequa]] and [[Jel-Novi]] to mine kalkite deposits. Rumors quickly spread across the planet, and following Kaido's suggestions, the Empire removed riot barriers at [[Palmo Plaza]], the site of the planet's [[Imperial office complex]], to lure in the Ghor. The next morning, Imperial forces, anticipating a protest, shut down comms and ordered Imperial employees to the office complex. Simultaneously, Palmo's residents, having heard the rumors, began marching to the plaza, chanting on the way there. The [[Ghorman Front]]'s leader, [[Carro Rylanz]], suspecting a trap, attempted to stop the protesters, but his efforts were in vain. After seeing [[Syril Karn]] in the crowd, Rylanz yanked him aside and attempted to question him about the presence of Imperial mining equipment on the planet, though Karn was also unaware of it, dismissing it as a rumor and stating that he was only there to stop outside agitators, before rejoining the crowd. [[File:WHO-StormtroopersCloseIn.png||thumb|left|250px|Imperial troops surrounded the now filled plaza, trapping the protesters]] Soon after, the plaza began to fill with protesters, and they continued to chant and wave flags. Simultaneously, Karn entered the Imperial office complex and questioned his partner and Ghorman project head, Dedra Meero. After learning the truth from her, Karn furiously left the building and reentered the crowd. Shortly after, Imperial troops surrounded the plaza, trapping the protesters in, as a set of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] took to the skies of Palmo. ===An Imperial brig=== {{Quote|Patrol, sir? Within the crowd?''"
"''Was that not my order?''"
"''They're green, sir. They're useless.''"
"''I see Imperial uniforms, Sergeant. I see a barricade lane to the Memorial that I need kept open. You will march them out there immediately and secure the area. Or you can all finish your days in an Imperial brig.|Bloy and Kaido|audio=Bloy-Kaido-Patrol-WhoAreYou.flac|{{Andor|Who Are You?}}}} [[File:GhormanMassacre-SecondShot-WhoAreYou.png|thumb|right|300px|Believing the shot came from protesters, imperial troops opened fire on protesters after a riot squad member was shot as part of a false flag operation]] Soon, Ghorman Front member Lezine began to sing the [[We Are the Ghor|Ghorman National Anthem]], with the rest of the crowd joining in. Simultaneously, Kaido ordered a [[Bloy's riot squad|riot squad]] lead by Sergeant [[Bloy]] to maintain a barricaded route from the office complex to the [[Monument to the Fallen]]. Unbeknownst to Bloy however, Kaido had devised a plan to have an [[Unidentified Imperial sniper|Imperial sniper]] take out a member of the squad. Despite Bloy's protests, the riot squad marched out into the plaza as the protesters continued to sing. As the squad inched further, they faced resistance from the crowd, who punched and threw various items at the squad. Dedra Meero then gave permission for a massacre to begin, and Kaido ordered the sniper to fire. [[Bloy]], having witnessed the death of one of his men, thinking that the shot had come from a protester, ordered his men to open fire on the masses, with Imperial troops surrounding and in the plaza quickly joining in. [[File:WHO-ChaosofGhorman.png|thumb|left|230px|Imperial troops fired indiscriminately on protesters, forcing many to attempt to flee]] As the gunfire from Imperial troops began to indiscriminately rain down on the protesters, protesters rushed for the exits only to find the exits blocked. Simultaneously, members of the Ghorman Front who had joined the protest began returning fire at some troops, with one group of front members attempting to clear an exit of Imperial troops. As the killing continued, Captain Kaido, calmly observing the slaughter from the IOC building, gave the order to release [[KX-series security droid]]s into the plaza, one of which quickly dispatched of Front member [[Enza Rylanz]], scaring most remaining Front members into fleeing. As a group of stormtroopers moved to a position close the [[Palmo Plaza hotel|Plaza's hotel]], [[Thela]], a hotel bellhop and secret member of the Ghorman Front, threw a [[C-25 fragmentation grenade]] at the stormtrooper's position, blowing up the troops close to the hotel. [[File:WhoAreYou-EpisodeThumbnail.png|thumb|right|250px|Syril Karn witnessed the chaos of the Ghorman Massacre that he unknowingly helped create]] Syril Karn, witnessing the aftermath of chaos that he had help create, spotted [[Axis network]] operative [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian Andor]], who had arrived to assassinate Dedra Meero. Karn attacked Cassian, tackling into the nearby [[Ghorman cafe|cafhouse]] and preventing the rebel from firing at Meero. In the resulting brawl, Karn nearly killed Andor, though after learning the rebel had no idea who he was, he froze in shock before being shot by Carro Rylanz. Following the brawl, Andor fled along with his accomplice [[Wilmon Paak]] alongside many protesters. The security droids soon proceeded out of the plaza as well, chasing and killing protesters across the streets of Palmo. As one [[K-2SO|security droid]] cornered Cassian Andor and some protestors, it was rammed and disabled by a hijacked [[Unidentified troop transport|repulsorcraft]] driven by Front Member [[Samm]]. Andor then had the KX droid’s remains put on the repulsorcraft, and fled Palmo. Simultaneously, Ghorman Front member [[Dreena]] and Wilmon Paak, sent broadcasts reporting the massacre unfolding in Palmo, desperately calling for help. By the end of the Massacre, thousands of Ghormans had been slaughtered by Imperial forces, with hundreds dead in Palmo Plaza alone. After the massacre, the Empire began mining the planet's kalkite deposits.{{Andor|Who Else Knows?}} ==Aftermath== ===Political fallout=== {{Main|Arrest of Dasi Oran|Escape from the Senate}} [[File:MonMothmaKnowntobeTrue-WelcometotheRebellion.png|thumb|left|300px|Senator Mon Mothma openly defied the Empire after the Ghorman Massacre, labelling it as a genocide.]] In the wake of the massacre, the Imperial-aligned media was quick to convey the Ghormans as the clear aggressors, just as an on-the-ground reporter had suggested and the pre-massacre planning had prepared for. Further, the news praised the Imperials who died as fallen patriots. All the same, the massacre exposed some [[journalist]]s to the lies told by the Empire. Among them were [[Corwi Selgrothe]], who defected from her position at [[HoloNet News]] in response to the massacre and went on to gain fame as a journalist for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. Nonetheless, the vast majority of Imperial News reinforced the anti-Ghorman narrative, which was also espoused by the majority of the Senate. In the immediate aftermath of the massacre, stormtroopers marched into the Senate Building and [[Arrest of Dasi Oran|arrested]] Ghorman senator Dasi Oran, who received no help from those watching on. Reports of the massacre reached [[Senator]] [[Tynnra Pamlo]], who worked closely with [[Rebel Alliance Intelligence Service]]. Senator Mothma, meanwhile, gave a speech in which she openly and publicly condemned the Empire's actions as a genocide and put the blame for the massacre on [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] himself, whom she labeled a monster, one which the very Senate had helped created. After giving her denouncement speech, Mothma [[Escape from the Senate|fled from the Empire]]. Mothma's words came as a shock to the Senate and received rage from loyalist senators, who branded her a traitor. ===Imperial response and analysis=== {{Quote|This attempt to crush dissent may have been a serious miscalculation by the Imperial officials who orchestrated it. Rather than terrify the wider civilian population into accepting Imperial rule, it showed many with rebel leanings that if even peaceful protest would be greeted with death, then there could be no political solution or compromise. If people were going to die regardless of how they resisted, then it may as well become an armed resistance.|Historian Beaumont Kin in ''The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire''|}} [[File:StrengthAndObedience-SWPropaganda.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Galactic Empire attempted to paint itself as a force of law and order that only used its might to protect its citizenry, but the Ghorman Massacre helped push the galaxy into rebellion.]] The Imperial response to the massacre included an insistence on law and order. [[Pollux Hax]], the [[Minister of Information]] for the [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order]],[[HoloNet News promotional pin]] stated in a broadcast on [[Imperial HoloVision]] after the massacre that "acceptance of Imperial law is the only way in which ordinary citizens can protect themselves from the dangers and violence of disorder." Historian [[Beaumont Kin]] later noted in his''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' book, ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'', that the attempt to crush dissent on Ghorman may have been a miscalculation by Imperial officials, who believed it would frighten civilians into acceptance of Imperial rule. Kin noted that, rather than succeeding, the Empire's actions—and the Empire's inability to discern between the peaceful tactics of protesters and the armed resistance of groups like the Partisans—prompted those with rebel leanings to realize that if peaceful protests would be greeted in the same way as violent action, there were no political solutions to be found and armed resistance was needed to combat Imperial rule. These actions, like the [[Declaration of the Rebel Alliance]], became consequential contributions to the Galactic Civil War. ===Rebel response=== {{Quote|This is Senator Mon Mothma, I have been called a traitor for speaking out against a corrupt Galactic Senate. A Senate manipulated by the sinister tactics of the Emperor. For too long I have watched the heavy hand of the Empire strangle our liberties, stifling our freedoms in the name of ensuring our safety. No longer! Despite Imperial threats, despite the Emperor himself, I have no fear as I take new action. For I am not alone. Beginning today we stand together as allies. I hereby resign from the Senate to fight for you, not from the distant hall of politics but from the front lines. We will not rest until we bring an end to the Empire, until we restore our Republic! Are you with me?|Mon Mothma to the various rebel cells|}} Following the massacre, [[Magva Yarro]], who had taken part in the protests, survived what happened on Ghorman and joined the Partisans.''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' The [[artist]] [[Mevera Starros]] [[Smuggler|smuggled]] a few cases of the beverage [[Sacha-Lo]] from Ghorman after the massacre and kept a few bottles for herself.[[Sana Starros 2|''Sana Starros'' 2]] After her initial speech in the senate and her escape from the Empire, Mothma delivered a further speech{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/why-andor-diverged-from-canon-mon-mothmas-epic-senate-speech-11729531|text=Andor star Genevieve O'Reilly and creator break down Mon Mothma's epic Senate speech, diverging from canon|author=Maureen Lee Lenker|date=2025-05-07|work=''Entertainment Weekly''|archivedate=20250507183159}} on the [[HoloNet]]{{DarthVaderCite|54|The Dark Side}} where she decried Palpatine as a "lying executioner" and squarely blamed him for the Ghorman Massacre. Her public actions prompted an Imperial Security Bureau investigation, and she was labeled a traitor to the Empire.''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' She was picked up by the rebel group known as the [[Spectres]], led by [[Phoenix Leader]] [[Hera Syndulla]], under orders from Senator Organa. The resulting skirmish with the Empire, in what became known as [[Operation Handoff]], saw the Spectres and the rebel [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]] bring Mothma to safety after a battle with pursuing Imperial forces in the [[Archeon Nebula]]. [[File:Secret_Cargo.jpg|thumb|250px|left|Mon Mothma, with the Spectres, gives the speech that became known as the Declaration of the Rebel Alliance.]] Mothma's rebel saviors brought her to [[Dantooine]], where a rebel base would be established.{{Film|IV}} Mothma broadcast the speech that became known as the Declaration of the Rebel Alliance, in which she resigned from the Imperial Senate, called out the Emperor's manipulative tactics, and decried the Empire's assault on freedom and liberty in the name of safety. She called on allies to stand together and begin taking the fight against the Empire to the front lines and restore the Republic. The broadcast, watched across the galaxy, inspired a [[Rebel Alliance Navy|rebel fleet]] to arrive at Dantooine. This event marked the formation of the Rebel Alliance, which kept documents pertaining to the massacre from Alliance leaders in ''[[The Rebel Files]]''. The Rebel Alliance ultimately went on to topple the Empire''[[Aftermath: Empire's End]]'' and establish the [[New Republic]], with Mothma as its first [[Chancellor (New Republic)|chancellor]].{{Ahsoka|Part Seven: Dreams and Madness}} ===Historical study=== {{Quote|Come with us to a city once rich in silk and twill, and learn about the Imperials' slow encroachment into everyday Ghor life, resulting in a massacre of peaceful civilians. A quiet mourning ceremony will take place after.|[[Century of Change tour]] itinerary|''[[Eyes Like Stars]]''}} The Ghorman Massacre was mentioned repeatedly throughout ''The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire'' due to the important role it played in recent galactic history. Beyond the analysis Beaumont Kin provided in the text about how the massacre impacted politics and the Galactic Civil War, he made sure to mention the massacre as an example of a major Imperial atrocity so as to inspire his readers to never allow another autocratic government to emerge. By the time ''The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire'' was published in [[35 ABY]],{{RiseAndFallDate}} the [[Memorial to the Missing of Ghorman]] had been established to honor those killed on Ghorman during the Imperial Era, including those lost during the Ghorman Massacre. Kin noted in his book that, because of the sheer death toll during the Empire's reign, information about many of Ghorman's casualties might never be known. ==Behind the scenes== ===Development=== {{Quote|Both sides are using this event for their own purposes. Krennic is obviously using it in a fascistic way to create a narrative in which the fear and the danger of radicals/anarchists needs to be crushed and stamped out at any cost—needs to be destroyed. Luthen understands that when you have 95% of the sentient beings of the universe who are not committed in any way to the struggle that's going on—they've decided for whatever reason that they're going to live with it and go along with it—Luthen realizes that he needs an event in which a line that's crossed is so egregious and so undemocratic and so morally wrong on its surface that people will be called to arms.|[[Dan Gilroy]], on the Ghorman Massacre serving as the "fulcrum" of ''Andor''|{{YouTube|video=Wyi0DanN6BU|text=Art & Crafts: Making of ‘Andor’ Season 2|channel=@The-Ankler|name=The Ankler|date=2025-08-25}}}} [[File:PalmoPlazaVFX.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Palmo Plaza, before and after the addition of visual effects]] The Ghorman Massacre was first mentioned in the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in ''[[Forged in Battle]]'', a [[2016]] sourcebook for [[Fantasy Flight Games]].''[[Forged in Battle]]'' The [[Ghorman Massacre/Legends|event]] originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first mentioned in ''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]'' by [[Paul Murphy]], released in [[1990]].''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]'' Murphy took influence from the real-world [[Wikipedia:Jallianwala Bagh massacre|Jallianwala Bagh massacre]] in [[1910s|1919]] when the [[Wikipedia:British Indian Army|British Indian Army]] surrounded and fired at hundreds of peaceful protestors at the [[Wikipedia:Jallianwala Bagh|Jallianwala Bagh]] in [[Wikipedia:Amritsar|Amritsar]] in [[Wikipedia:Punjab, India|Punjab, India]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.theringer.com/2025/05/08/star-wars/andor-lore-star-wars-rpg-history-ghorman-massacre-paul-murphy-west-end-games|text=The Roots of ‘Andor’ Lore Run Deep|author=Lindbergh, Ben|date=2025-05-09|work=[[Wikipedia:The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]|archivedate=20250609215800}} Instead of the canon date of 2 BBY, the original Legends event occurred early into the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]] in c. [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' It also notably featured [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] landing his [[Starship/Legends|starship]] on a group of protesters blocking its landing pad.[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook (Second Edition)|''The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook'', Second Edition]] The event inspired [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] to join Senator [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] in plotting a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|rebellion]] against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]]. In the [[Andor Season 2|second season]] of the live-action [[Disney+]] television series [[Star Wars: Andor|''Andor'']], the Legends version of the event is confirmed to still have occurred in 19 BBY as a separate event named the [[Tarkin Massacre]],{{Andor|Ever Been to Ghorman?}} though it is not the canon Ghorman Massacre that was depicted later in the season. The event made its first ever on-screen appearance in "[[Who Are You?]]," the eighth episode of the second season of the television series ''Andor'', released on [[May 6]], [[2025]].{{SW|url=news/andor-season-2-teaser-trailer-key-art-reveal|text=First ''Andor A Star Wars Story'' Teaser Trailer and Poster Revealed}} Showrunner [[Tony Gilroy]] had previously affirmed in [[2022]] that he knew of the event and how it was on the horizon for Mothma.{{YouTube|video=X13nYZNTLYM|text=Andor Q&A - Tony Gilroy - (S1 eps 1-4 )|channel=backstorymagazine2757|name=Backstory Magazine|date=2022-09-29}} It was first shown in a short teaser released on [[November 12]], [[2024]]{{DisneyPlusYouTube|gnwpxgR3STE|Coming in 2025 | Disney+|nolive=1}} and was first properly identified as such in an interview with Gilroy released on [[March 10]], 2025. Gilroy stated that the event's appearance in the series, told over the course of five episodes, will have "straightened out that story" as there had been "a lot of confusion within canon" about the Ghorman Massacre.{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/andor-season-2-preview-tony-gilroy-collateral-damage|text=“I Want To Make the Show Timeless”: Tony Gilroy Previews ’Andor Season 2 and the “Collateral Damage” Ahead|author=Maggie Lovitt|date=2025-03-10|archivedate=20250310200653|work=''[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|Collider]]''}} The depiction of the Ghorman Massacre in ''Andor'' Season 2 was one of the challenges tackled by supervising sound editor and [[Wikipedia:Dubbing|ADR]] supervisor [[Margit Pfeiffer]] of [[Skywalker Sound]]. She was tasked with finding and conducting crowd noises that spoke in the [[Ghor (language)|Ghor]] language invented for the series. As the events on Ghorman intensified, she created the sound to intensify and escale in its energy, complete with singing, callouts, and panicked cries, with chants continuing throughout the events that were designed to weave in and out of the sound design for the battle before reaching a crescendo into the singing of the Ghorman National Anthem. The season's musical composer, [[Nicholas Britell]], worked with Gilroy to develop the Ghorman National Anthem before the second season filmed, with their goal being to create something that felt like a timeless, authentic, and emotional rallying cry. Indeed, "the galaxy is watching" cry was chosen by Gilroy because it echoed the real world "the whole world is watching" protest phrase, which has seen use since the 1950s and thus, in Gilroy's words, was "universal enough" to be borrowed by the show.{{WebCite|url=https://mashable.com/article/andor-galaxy-watching|text='The galaxy is watching!' How 'Andor' connects to a history of protest|author=Chris Taylor Lambie|date=2025-05-07|work=[[Wikipedia:Mashable|''Mashable'']]|archivedate=20250508050855}} [[Eugene Lin]], who portrayed an Imperial security trooper in the Ghorman Massacre, compared its events to the [[Wikipedia:1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre|Tiananmen Square protests and massacre]].{{Instagram|username=andor.imperial.officer|name=[[Eugene Lin]]|nolive=1}} ===Contradictions and retcons=== {{Quote|I'm ''really'' confident that the really deep, passionate Star Wars community will appreciate how we've straightened out that story.|Tony Gilroy on the Ghorman Massacre's depiction in the second season of ''Andor''|}} The book ''[[The Mighty Chewbacca in the Forest of Fear!]]'' mentions when Cassian Andor stole [[K-2SO]],''[[The Mighty Chewbacca in the Forest of Fear!]]'' which at the time would have been a reference to the [[mission to Wecacoe]] from [[Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special 1|''Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special'' 1]].[[Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special 1|''Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special'' 1]] However the [[Star Wars: Andor|''Andor'']] episode "[[Who Are You?]]" featured an alternate backstory where Andor stole K2 during the Ghorman Massacre. As ''Andor'' is intended to override the comic,{{YouTube|video=4Hk3w9W0ZjA|text=Tony Gilroy talks ANDOR, STAR WARS, BOURNE, MICHAEL CLAYTON I Happy Sad Confused|channel=JoshHorowitz|name=Josh Horowitz}} meaning the reference to the theft of K2 in ''The Mighty Chewbacca'' [[Retroactive continuity|retroactively]] is a reference to the Ghorman Massacre. ==Appearances== {{Indexpage}} {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of the Ghorman Massacre}} *{{Andor|Who Are You?}} {{1st}} {{1stID|Imperial murder of Ghorman}} *{{Andor|Welcome to the Rebellion}} {{Mo}} *{{Rebels|Secret Cargo}} {{Mo}} *''[[The Mighty Chewbacca in the Forest of Fear!]]'' {{Ab|The Mighty Chewbacca in the Forest of Fear!
